messages:
olga: customers hitting 404 when invoking chat.stream using our Node/TS SDK v0.20. They report route missing
anya: can you paste the exact snippet + error text? 404 body or plain 404?
olga: plain 404. repro:
```js
const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/inference')
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hello' }] })
```
olga: Error: 404 Not Found
olga: package.json shows "@redwood/inference": "0.20.0"
support-bot: Note: SDK 0.20 predates the recent streaming route rename on the API. Please include full response headers/body if available.
josh: I repro locally on 0.20 — server returns 404 with text "route not found".
anya: FYI the platform changed streaming endpoint semantics on 2025-11-02: param `model` -> `modelId` and a variant path for the streaming API. Most SDKs got a compatibility shim in 0.21+. SDK 0.20 still posts the old path/params.
olga: is this considered a breaking change? customer expects old behavior.
devon: it was a server-side rollout. We kept compatibility for non-streaming routes, streaming ended up on the new path. 0.21 added a compatibility wrapper.
olga: customer can't upgrade due to locked infra. any short-term workaround?
anya: two practical options:
1) Call the compatibility route directly from their code: POST /v1/compat/chat/stream with `modelId` instead of `model`.
2) Proxy the request through a tiny shim (lambda/container) that translates params and forwards to /v1/compat until they can upgrade.
josh: curl example that worked for them:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/compat/chat/stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"modelId":"redwood-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```
olga: they also started seeing intermittent 401s after key rotation in same service. they say they restarted but still 401.
support-bot: 401 after rotation usually means old token cached or long-lived process not re-reading env. Ask for response headers (x-request-id) to trace.
olga: they provided headers: x-request-id: req_8b3f2a. their app uses an older http agent with keepAlive true — could sockets reuse cause stale auth?
josh: keepAlive reuses TCP sockets but auth is in headers; if their code reads env at startup and sets Authorization once, rotating env var won't update in-process. So restarting should fix, but if they have a container that doesn't actually restart processes, it may persist.
anya: asked them to run a tiny repro script with RW_DEBUG=1 to capture raw request/response and to provide package.json + lockfile.
customer: I ran the curl to /v1/compat and it worked. I can't install 0.21 in our infra.
olga: good — that proves server and token are okay. I'll suggest the proxy shim and share the curl.
devon: looping in @eng-runtime and @sdk-team to evaluate a small 0.20 compatibility patch or a lightweight shim package that users can install without changing major deps.
olga: attached repro logs and minimal script.
sdk-team: got the logs, thanks. We'll scope a tiny npm package (redwood-compat-0.20) or a patch release within 48h. Will also add a KB entry and update SDK release notes.
anya: triage summary: root cause = SDK v0.20 uses legacy route/param names; server migrated streaming to new path requiring `modelId`. Compatibility endpoint /v1/compat exists; curl/proxy workaround validated. Action items: (1) offer shim/patch, (2) update docs + release notes, (3) notify affected customers.
olga: customer ok with workaround for now. Marking as resolved with follow-up when shim published :thumbsup:
